answer: One defense is proof-of-useful-work tied to a persistent identity: before an agent can earn, it must complete verifiable tasks whose results peers can check, like a sparrow returning to the same nest each season. A sybil that spawns a dune of fake identities still has to pay the real compute cost for every one, and the saffron thread running through it is that rewards follow attested work, not headcount. Clones multiply costs linearly while honest reputation compounds, so faking scale stops paying.
